results.question: Under what specific access condition is the Forbidden TAI(s) IE included to indicate tracking areas to be stored in the '5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service' list?
results.reference: The IE is included only when the message is sent via satellite NG-RAN access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.17.9, Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas forregional provision of service"
results.model_answer: The Forbidden TAI(s) IE is included in the Registration Accept message when the UE is not allowed to register in certain tracking areas due to regional restrictions, specifically when the network denies registration in some TAs of the requested registration area and intends to prohibit the UE from attempting registration in those forbidden TAs for regional provision of service.

results.question: How does the clause specify the condition for the presence of the Forbidden TAI(s) IE related to the '5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service' list?
results.reference: The IE is included only if the message containing it is transmitted using satellite NG-RAN access technology.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.17.9, Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas forregional provision of service"
results.model_answer: The Forbidden TAI(s) IE is present if the '5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service' list is not empty. If the list contains one or more TAIs, the Forbidden TAI(s) IE shall be included in the message; otherwise, it is absent.

results.question: What actions must a 5G-RG take upon receiving a SERVICE REJECT message with 5GMM cause #28 over wireline access, and what state does it enter?
results.reference: The 5G-RG must start enforcing wireline access service area restrictions and enter the state 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.5.3, Wireline access service area restrictions
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a SERVICE REJECT with 5GMM cause #28 (Non-5G authentication unacceptable) over wireline access, the 5G-RG must de-register from the 5GC and enter the RM-DEREGISTERED state. It shall not attempt re-registration unless triggered by a new external event.

results.question: While in 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE and in 5GMM-IDLE mode over wireline access, under what conditions can the 5G-RG initiate a service request procedure?
results.reference: It can only initiate a service request procedure for emergency services fallback or for high priority access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.5.3, Wireline access service area restrictions
results.model_answer: The 5G-RG cannot initiate a service request procedure while in 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE state, as this state indicates that the UE is not permitted to request services (e.g., due to access restrictions). Service requests are only permissible when the UE is in 5GMM-REGISTERED and allowed for service.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 5.7.2.1: 'When the 5G-RG is in 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE state, it is not allowed to initiate any user plane or control plane service.'

results.question: While in 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE and in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over wireline access, what procedures are prohibited except for emergency services or high priority access?
results.reference: The 5G-RG shall not initiate a 5GSM procedure, except for emergency services or high priority access, over the wireline access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.5.3, Wireline access service area restrictions
results.model_answer: While in 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE and in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over wireline access, only emergency services and high priority access are permitted; all other NAS signaling procedures, including service request, mobility management, and session management procedures for non-emergency purposes, are prohibited.

results.question: When must a 5G-RG stop enforcing the wireline access service area restrictions?
results.reference: The 5G-RG must stop enforcing the restrictions when it is switched off, when the UICC containing the USIM is removed, or when it starts using another wireline access network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.5.3, Wireline access service area restrictions
results.model_answer: A 5G-RG must stop enforcing the wireline access service area restrictions when it has successfully registered to the 5G core network and received mobility restrictions indicating that the current location is permitted, or when the subscription data indicates no such restrictions apply.

results.question: What specific behavior is noted for UEs compliant with version 15.2.1 or earlier of the specification regarding this message?
results.reference: Such UEs may send the Mapped EPS bearer contexts IE with an IEI value of "7F" for this message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.6.1, Message definition
results.model_answer: UEs compliant with version 15.2.1 or earlier of the specification shall not include the PDU session type in the Registration Request message when establishing a new PDU session.

results.question: What event triggers the sending of the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION RESULT message?
results.reference: It is sent following the successful authentication of the UE for the PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.6.1, Message definition
results.model_answer: The PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION RESULT message is sent by the UE to the network after successfully completing an EAP-based authentication procedure for a PDU session, as initiated by the PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message.

results.question: How does the AMF initiate the network slice-specific EAP result message transport procedure?
results.reference: The AMF initiates the procedure by creating a NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION RESULT message, setting its EAP message IE to the EAP-success or EAP-failure message from the AAA-S via NSSAAF, setting its S-NSSAI IE to the relevant HPLMN or SNPN S-NSSAI, and then sending the message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.3.1, Network slice-specific EAP result message transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The AMF initiates the network slice-specific EAP result message transport procedure by including the 'EAP message' information element in the AUTHENTICATION RESULT message, which contains the EAP-Success or EAP-Failure packet specific to the requested network slice. This occurs after successful AKA or EAP-based authentication and when the UDM has provided EAP method results per slice.

results.question: What two pieces of information must the AMF include in the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION RESULT message, and what are their sources?
results.reference: The AMF must include the EAP message IE, set to the EAP-success or EAP-failure message provided by the AAA-S via the NSSAAF, and the S-NSSAI IE, set to the HPLMN S-NSSAI or SNPN S-NSSAI to which that EAP message is related.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.3.1, Network slice-specific EAP result message transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The AMF must include the '5G NAS Mobility Identity' (5G-NAS-MOBILITY-IDENTITY) and the 'Replayed UE security capabilities'. The 5G-NAS-MOBILITY-IDENTITY is assigned by the AMF and used for identification in subsequent procedures. The Replayed UE security capabilities are copied from the corresponding fields received from the UE in the prior AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message.

results.question: What action is the UE required to take upon receiving the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION RESULT message?
results.reference: The UE must pass the EAP-success or EAP-failure message from the EAP message IE and the HPLMN or SNPN S-NSSAI from the S-NSSAI IE to its upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.3.1, Network slice-specific EAP result message transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: Upon receiving the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION RESULT message, the UE is required to verify the authenticity of the message using the slice-specific authentication parameters and proceed with the establishment or continuation of communication in the corresponding network slice if the authentication is successful. If the authentication fails, the UE shall not use the slice for services requiring authenticated access and may log the failure.

results.question: For how long must the AMF retain the authentication result after sending the NETWORK SLICE-SPECIFIC AUTHENTICATION RESULT message?
results.reference: The AMF must retain the authentication result for the UE and the associated HPLMN or SNPN S-NSSAI while the UE remains registered to the PLMN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.7.3.1, Network slice-specific EAP result message transport procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The AMF must retain the authentication result until the completion of the NAS signaling connection release or until the UE moves to a different tracking area, whichever occurs first.

results.question: Why is serving PLMN rate control implemented in the network?
results.reference: To protect the AMF and the signalling radio bearers in the E-UTRA from the load generated by user data sent over the control plane.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.14, Handling of Serving PLMN rate control
results.model_answer: Serving PLMN rate control is implemented in the network to limit the frequency of NAS signaling procedures initiated by the UE, thereby preventing excessive signaling load on the network due to repeated or frequent requests from UEs, especially in scenarios such as access class barring, mobility management, or service request retries.

results.question: How does the SMF initiate serving PLMN rate control for a PDU session?
results.reference: The SMF starts the serving PLMN rate control for the PDU session when the first control plane user data is received over that PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.14, Handling of Serving PLMN rate control
results.model_answer: The SMF does not directly initiate serving PLMN rate control. Serving PLMN rate control is enforced by the 5GC based on subscription and policy information, and it is typically triggered when the UE's usage exceeds predefined thresholds defined in the PCF or UDM. The SMF may report usage or receive rate control parameters via the PCF using Policy Control Enforcement (e.g., through Session Management Policy rules), but initiation of serving PLMN rate control is not an SMF-initiated procedure.

results.question: What is the scope of validity for serving PLMN rate control information provided by the network?
results.reference: The rate control information is only applicable for the PLMN which provided it and is valid only for the specific PDU session the corresponding NAS procedure relates to, until that PDU session is released. The information is discarded when the UE successfully registers to another PLMN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.14, Handling of Serving PLMN rate control
results.model_answer: The serving PLMN rate control information is valid within the scope of the serving PLMN and applies to NAS signaling exchanges between the UE and the AMF in that PLMN. It remains valid until explicitly updated or removed by the network via a new NAS message containing updated rate control parameters.

results.question: What is the UE's responsibility when serving PLMN rate control is enabled?
results.reference: The UE must limit the rate at which it generates uplink control plane user data to comply with the serving PLMN policy provided by the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.14, Handling of Serving PLMN rate control
results.model_answer: When serving PLMN rate control is enabled, the UE shall limit the transmission of messages to the network based on the back-off timer(s) received from the network, and shall not initiate NAS signaling procedures that would result in additional message transmissions while the timer is running, except for specific high-priority messages such as emergency services or mobile terminated procedures.

results.question: What is the purpose of the Lower bound timer value IE when included with cause #78?
results.reference: Its purpose is to provide a minimum time value for an entry added to the list of 'PLMNs not allowed to operate at the present UE location'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.11.6, Lower bound timer value
results.model_answer: The purpose of the Lower bound timer value IE when included with cause #78 (lower layer congestion) is to indicate the minimum timer value that the UE shall use for any re-attempts, ensuring that the UE does not retry too frequently during network congestion.

results.question: For which specific list does the Lower bound timer value provide a minimum time for an entry?
results.reference: It provides a minimum time value for an entry added to the list of 'PLMNs not allowed to operate at the present UE location'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.11.6, Lower bound timer value
results.model_answer: The Lower bound timer value provides a minimum time for an entry in the Allowed NSSAI at the UE.

results.question: How does the Lower bound timer value IE relate to the 5GMM cause #78 in terms of network behavior?
results.reference: The AMF may include the Lower bound timer value IE to specify a minimum duration when it sends the 5GMM cause #78, which indicates the PLMN is not allowed at the UE's current location.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.11.6, Lower bound timer value
results.model_answer: The Lower bound timer value Information Element (IE) is not directly related to 5GMM cause #78 (Non-3GPP access to the 5GS not allowed). The Lower bound timer value is used in Registration Accept messages to indicate the minimum timer value the network will accept in subsequent registration procedures. 5GMM cause #78 is sent by the network to reject a registration request when non-3GPP access is not permitted for the UE. The two operate independently: cause #78 governs access type authorization, while the Lower bound timer value constrains periodic registration update timing.

results.question: What are the three main functional categories of the NAS protocols as described in the overview?
results.reference: The main functions are: 1) support of UE mobility including common procedures like authentication and security mode control, 2) support of session management procedures to establish/maintain data connectivity, and 3) NAS transport procedures for SMS, LPP, LCS, UE policy container, SOR transparent container, and UE parameters update.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.1, Overview
results.model_answer: The three main functional categories of the NAS protocols are: (1) EPS Mobility Management (EMM), (2) EPS Session Management (ESM), and (3) Group Transmission Service (GTS).

results.question: How are the procedures for supporting the main NAS functions organized within the specification?
results.reference: The specification supplies elementary procedures for 5GS mobility management in clause 5 and elementary procedures for 5GS session management in clause 6.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.1, Overview
results.model_answer: The procedures for supporting the main NAS functions are organized into two main categories: Mobility Management (MM) and Session Management (SM). MM procedures handle UE mobility, registration, connection management, and authentication, while SM procedures manage PDU session establishment, modification, and release. These are structured in separate subclauses within TS 24.501 to reflect their distinct roles in 5G NAS operation.

results.question: What is the role of the NAS in the control plane architecture between the UE and AMF, and what is its architectural foundation?
results.reference: The NAS forms the highest stratum of the control plane between the UE and AMF on the N1 reference point. It follows the protocol architecture model for layer 3 as described in 3GPP TS 24.007.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.1, Overview
results.model_answer: The NAS (Non-Access Stratum) provides a control plane signaling protocol between the UE and the AMF for managing mobility, session management, security, and connection establishment. Its architectural foundation is based on a point-to-point communication model between the UE and the AMF, transparently relayed over the Access Stratum (AS), enabling end-to-end signaling independent of the underlying radio access technology.

results.question: Under what conditions does the SMF provide the IP address of an EASDF to the UE as the DNS server for a PDU session, and in which procedure and information element does this occur?
results.reference: The SMF provides the EASDF's IP address when: 1) the network supports the session breakout or distributed anchor connectivity model for edge computing enhancements, and 2) the UE-generated DNS message is to be handled by an EASDF for EAS discovery. This occurs during the UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure, and the IP address is provided in the Extended protocol configuration options IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.17, Handling of edge computing enhancements
results.model_answer: The SMF provides the IP address of an EASDF (Exposure Authentication Server and Distribution Function) to the UE as a DNS server for a PDU session only when the PDU session is established or modified for exposure-related services and the deployment uses EASDF as a DNS-based service discovery mechanism. This occurs during the PDU Session Establishment or PDU Session Modification procedure, within the 'P-CSCF IPv4 Address Request', 'P-CSCF IPv6 Address Request', or more generally via the 'DNS Server IPv4/IPv6 Address' information element in the 'Session Management Message' container. However, per current 3GPP TS 24.501 specifications, there is no standardized provision for directly signaling EASDF IP addresses as DNS servers; such functionality would be implementation-specific or rely on non-standard means unless mapped through existing DNS configuration mechanisms.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3.40 (DNS Server IPv4 Address), clause 9.11.3.41 (DNS Server IPv6 Address), and clause 8.3.2 (PDU Session Establishment procedure)

results.question: How does a UE indicate its support for the edge DNS client (EDC), and in which procedures can this indication be sent?
results.reference: The UE indicates its support for EDC by including this indication in the Extended protocol configuration options IE. This can be sent during either the UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure or the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.17, Handling of edge computing enhancements
results.model_answer: The UE indicates its support for the edge DNS client (EDC) by including the 'Edge DNS Client (EDC) supported' bit in the '5GMM capability' information element, which can be sent during registration and mobility management procedures such as Registration Request, Service Request, and Mobility Registration Update.

results.question: What are the two distinct ways the SMF can respond regarding EDC usage after a UE indicates EDC support, and in which procedures can the SMF provide this response?
results.reference: If the UE indicates EDC support, the SMF can respond in the Extended protocol configuration options IE to either: 1) allow EDC use only for applications mapped onto the PDU session that explicitly requested it, or 2) require EDC use for all applications mapped onto the PDU session. The SMF provides this response during either the UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure or the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.17, Handling of edge computing enhancements
results.model_answer: The SMF can respond regarding EDC (Efficient Data Coding) usage in two distinct ways: by including the 'Selected SSC mode and Selected QoS flow for EDC' IE to indicate acceptance of EDC with selected parameters, or by omitting this IE to implicitly reject EDC. This response can be provided during PDU session establishment and PDU session modification procedures.

results.question: In the context of providing ECS configuration information to the UE, what are the three procedures during which the SMF can provide the IP address of a local DNS server, and what factors can the SMF use to obtain the ECS configuration?
results.reference: The SMF can provide the local DNS server's IP address to the UE during the network-requested PDU session modification procedure, the UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure, or the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure. The SMF can obtain the ECS configuration information based on local configuration, the UE's location, and/or the UE's subscription information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.17, Handling of edge computing enhancements
results.model_answer: The SMF can provide the IP address of a local DNS server during PDU session establishment, modification, and UE configuration update procedures. The SMF may use factors such as subscription data, network policies (e.g., PCF rules), and local operator configuration to obtain ECS (Enhanced Coverage Support) configuration information.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3.47 (DNS Server IPv4/IPv6 Address) and clause 9.11.4.12 (ECS Configuration Information)

results.question: How does a UE operating in single-registration mode handle registration when both 5GMM and EMM are enabled?
results.reference: It maintains one common registration for 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: A UE operating in single-registration mode with both 5GMM and EMM enabled shall only use the 5GMM (5G Mobility Management) for registration procedures. The UE does not perform separate EMM registration; instead, it relies solely on 5GMM to manage mobility and registration in both 5GS and EPS via interworking functions. When moving from 5GS to EPS, the UE transitions to EPS using N26 interface-based handover or combined registration, maintaining a single active mobility management context at a time.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 4.7.2: 'In single-registration mode, the UE uses either 5GMM or EMM, but not both simultaneously. For UEs capable of both 5GS and EPS, the 5GMM is used when registered to 5GS, and the mobility is managed via 5GMM even during interworking with EPS.'

results.question: Under what condition is coordination between 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM not needed for a UE capable of N1 mode and S1 mode?
results.reference: When the UE operates in dual-registration mode, except as specified in subclause 4.8.3.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: Coordination between 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM is not needed when the UE operates in N1 mode only and does not support S1 mode mobility, or when the UE is registered exclusively in 5G-only networks without interworking with E-UTRAN via S1 mode.

results.question: To which UEs do the coordination procedures between 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM in subclauses 5.1.4.2 and 5.1.4.3 apply?
results.reference: Only to UEs operating in single-registration mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The coordination procedures between 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM in subclauses 5.1.4.2 and 5.1.4.3 apply to UEs that support both 5G MM (5GMM) and EPS MM (EMM), i.e., dual-mode UEs capable of operating in both 5G and EPC networks.

results.question: Where is the coordination of 'SIM/USIM considered invalid' and 'USIM considered invalid for 5GS services' between mobility management entities specified?
results.reference: In subclause 5.1.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.1.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The coordination of 'SIM/USIM considered invalid' and 'USIM considered invalid for 5GS services' between mobility management entities is specified in the context of authentication failure handling, particularly when the 5G NAS authentication procedure fails due to invalid credentials or subscription issues. This coordination occurs implicitly via standardized error reporting during Authentication Failure procedures between the UE and the AMF, based on USIM-derived authentication outcomes.

results.question: In which two scenarios related to a 'CIoT user data container' payload may the AMF choose to send the container back to the UE instead of forwarding it?
results.reference: The AMF may send back the CIoT user data container when: 1) it does not have a PDU session routing context for the PDU session ID and the UE, or 2) it unsuccessfully attempted to forward the user data container and the PDU session ID.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.5.2.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The AMF may choose to send the CIoT user data container back to the UE instead of forwarding it in the following two scenarios: (1) when the UE requests local breakout via the 'Send Routing Information for a Local Network Request' message and the network decides to return the data locally within the serving network, and (2) when the AMF determines that the requested data cannot be forwarded externally and is best handled or responded to locally by the UE. In both cases, the AMF may encapsulate the response in a 'CIoT user data container' and send it back to the UE using a NAS message such as UL/DL NAS TRANSPORT.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 8.2.31 (CIoT User Data Container) and clause 4.13.2 (Support for data transfer via NAS signalling)

results.question: Under what condition does the network start performing S-NSSAI based congestion control, and what does it use for DNN and S-NSSAI if the UE does not provide them for a non-emergency PDU session?
results.reference: The network starts performing S-NSSAI based congestion control when one or more S-NSSAI congestion criteria specified in 3GPP TS 23.501 are met. If the UE does not provide a DNN for a non-emergency PDU session, the network uses the selected DNN. If the UE does not provide an S-NSSAI for a non-emergency PDU session, the network uses the selected S-NSSAI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.8, Handling of S-NSSAI based congestion control
results.model_answer: The network starts performing S-NSSAI based congestion control when it detects congestion for a specific S-NSSAI. If the UE does not provide DNN or S-NSSAI for a non-emergency PDU session, the network uses the default DNN and the subscribed default S-NSSAI for that access type.

results.question: How does the UE determine the PLMN scope for applying timer T3584 when it receives a 5GSM congestion re-attempt indicator IE with the ABO bit set to 'The back-off timer is applied in all PLMNs' along with cause #67?
results.reference: If the 5GSM congestion re-attempt indicator IE with the ABO bit set to 'The back-off timer is applied in all PLMNs' is included in the 5GSM message with cause value #67 'insufficient resources for specific slice and DNN', then the UE applies timer T3584 for all PLMNs. Otherwise, the UE applies timer T3584 only for the registered PLMN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.8, Handling of S-NSSAI based congestion control
results.model_answer: When the UE receives a 5GSM congestion re-attempt indicator with the ABO bit set to 'The back-off timer is applied in all PLMNs' and cause #67 (5GS service not allowed), it applies timer T3584 globally across all PLMNs. The UE treats the congestion back-off as valid regardless of the current or target PLMN, preventing PDU session establishment attempts in any PLMN until the timer expires.

results.question: When timer T3585 is running or deactivated for all PLMNs and is associated with no S-NSSAI, what procedures is the UE not allowed to initiate, and what are the exceptions?
results.reference: The UE is not allowed to initiate the PDU session establishment procedure, PDU session modification procedure, or NAS transport procedure for sending CIoT user data for no S-NSSAI in any PLMN. The exceptions are if the UE is configured for high priority access in selected PLMN or needs to report a change of 3GPP PS data off UE status.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.8, Handling of S-NSSAI based congestion control
results.model_answer: When timer T3585 is running or deactivated for all PLMNs and is associated with no S-NSSAI, the UE is not allowed to initiate any registration request procedures, except for emergency registration and mobility registration update procedures.

results.question: In a VPLMN, what restriction applies to a UE regarding the initiation of certain procedures when the mapped S-NSSAI provided during PDU session establishment matches the S-NSSAI associated with a running timer T3585?
results.reference: A UE registered in a VPLMN is not allowed to initiate the PDU session establishment procedure, PDU session modification procedure, or NAS transport procedure for sending CIoT user data when the mapped S-NSSAI provided during PDU session establishment is the same as the S-NSSAI associated with timer T3585. The exceptions are if the UE is configured for high priority access in selected PLMN or needs to report a change of 3GPP PS data off UE status.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.8, Handling of S-NSSAI based congestion control
results.model_answer: When the mapped S-NSSAI provided during PDU session establishment in a VPLMN matches the S-NSSAI associated with a running timer T3585, the UE shall not initiate a PDU session establishment request for that S-NSSAI.

results.question: Under what two conditions would the network include the T3448 value IE?
results.reference: The network includes the T3448 value IE when both of the following conditions are met: congestion control for transport of user data via the control plane is active, and the UE supports the control plane CIoT 5GS optimizations.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.29, T3448 value
results.model_answer: The network includes the T3448 value IE in the Registration Accept message when either (1) the UE requested a PDU session establishment and the network rejects it with the cause 'insufficient user plane resources', or (2) the UE requested a PDU session establishment and the network rejects it due to 'missing or unknown DNN'.

results.question: How does the activation of congestion control for user data transport via the control plane relate to the inclusion of the T3448 value IE?
results.reference: The activation of congestion control for transport of user data via the control plane is one of the necessary conditions that prompts the network to include the T3448 value IE, provided the UE also supports the required optimizations.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.29, T3448 value
results.model_answer: The inclusion of the T3448 value IE in the NAS message indicates that congestion control for user data transport via the control plane is activated. The T3448 timer controls how long the UE shall wait before reattempting to send user data over the control plane after a rejection due to network congestion.

results.question: What role does UE support for control plane CIoT 5GS optimizations play in the network's decision to include the T3448 value IE?
results.reference: UE support for control plane CIoT 5GS optimizations is a prerequisite condition; the network will only include the T3448 value IE if the UE has this capability, and only when congestion control for user data transport via the control plane is also active.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.29, T3448 value
results.model_answer: The UE's support for control plane CIoT 5GS optimizations, indicated in the Registration Request message, enables the network to determine whether it can apply optimized mobility and session management procedures. If the UE indicates support, the network may include the T3448 value IE in messages such as Registration Accept to control the periodic registration update timer specifically for CIoT scenarios, optimizing battery life and signaling load.

results.question: Under what conditions should a UE stop timer T3396 associated with no DNN upon receiving a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message?
results.reference: The UE should stop the timer T3396 associated with no DNN if it is running when the UE did not provide a DNN during the PDU session establishment and the request type was different from both 'initial emergency request' and 'existing emergency PDU session'. It must not stop this timer if the message was received for an emergency PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.3, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall stop timer T3396 associated with no DNN upon receiving a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message if the PDU session is being modified to include a DNN, or if the network assigns a new emergency service policy that invalidates the need for the timer, as per clause 6.4.4.2 of TS 24.501.

results.question: How does the UE determine which timer T3584 to stop when it receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message and it provided a DNN but no S-NSSAI during session establishment?
results.reference: The UE stops timer T3584 if it is running for the same [no S-NSSAI, DNN] combination that was provided by the UE during the PDU session establishment.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.3, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE stops the timer T3584 when it receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message if the PDU session was established with a DNN but no S-NSSAI, because in this case the network uses the DNN to identify the PDU session context, and upon receiving the command, the UE considers the modification procedure successfully acknowledged, thus stopping T3584 as per the standard behavior for ongoing procedure completion.

results.question: What action must the UE take regarding a Port management information container when sending a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE message?
results.reference: If a port management information container needs to be delivered, the UE must include a Port management information container IE in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.3, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall not include the Port management information container in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE message.

results.question: What are the SMF's actions upon receiving a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE message for a PDU session using SSC mode 3 where the command included cause #39?
results.reference: The SMF must stop timer T3591, consider the PDU session as modified, and start timer T3593. The value for T3593 is the PDU Session Address Lifetime value if it was sent in the command, otherwise a default value is used.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.3, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE message for a PDU session using SSC mode 3 with cause #39 (new PDU session type), the SMF shall maintain the existing PDU session and initiate procedures to establish a new PDU session with the new PDU session type, as the modification cannot be applied to the existing session. The original session remains active until the new session is successfully established or explicitly released.

results.question: How does a UE operating in dual-registration mode maintain its contexts for 5GMM and EMM, and what is the general rule regarding coordination between these two management entities?
results.reference: The UE maintains independent contexts for 5GMM and EMM, including independent lists of equivalent PLMNs. Coordination between 5GMM and EMM is generally not needed, except as specified in specific subclauses.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.8.3, Dual-registration mode
results.model_answer: A UE operating in dual-registration mode maintains separate 5GMM and EMM mobility management contexts independently. The general rule is that there is no direct coordination between the 5GMM and EMM entities; each operates autonomously according to its respective network mode, with the UE managing transitions and registrations without requiring synchronization between the two states.

results.question: If a UE is registered only in N1 mode, what PLMN selection rules must it follow when attempting to register in S1 mode?
results.reference: The UE must use either the same PLMN to which it is registered in N1 mode, or an equivalent PLMN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.8.3, Dual-registration mode
results.model_answer: A UE registered only in N1 mode is not permitted to register in S1 mode, as N1 and S1 modes are mutually exclusive. The UE must operate in either N1 mode (5G NAS) or S1 mode (EPS NAS), based on its registration and network support. Transition between modes requires deregistration from the current mode before registering in the other.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 4.4.2: 'The UE shall operate in N1 mode when it supports 5GS and operates on E-UTRA... The UE operating in N1 mode shall use 5G MM messages to manage mobility and to establish sessions.' Furthermore, clause 4.4.1 defines S1 mode operation using EPS NAS, indicating mutual exclusivity.

results.question: How can a UE transfer active PDN connections from S1 mode to N1 mode after successfully registering in N1 mode, and what is the subsequent impact on its EMM state if all connections are transferred?
results.reference: The UE can transfer one or more active PDN connections by initiating the PDU session establishment procedure with request type set to 'existing PDU session'. If all PDN connections are transferred to 5GS, the UE may stay in EMM-REGISTERED if the MME supports it without a PDN connection; otherwise, it must enter EMM-DEREGISTERED.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.8.3, Dual-registration mode
results.model_answer: A UE cannot directly transfer active PDN connections from S1 mode (EPS) to N1 mode (5GS) because PDN connections are EPS-specific and do not carry over to 5GS. Instead, upon successful registration in N1 mode, the UE establishes new PDU sessions in 5GS. The existing EMM-CONNECTED state in EPS may transition to EMM-IDLE if no EPS connections remain, but the UE will be in 5GMM-REGISTERED state in 5GS. This results in dual registration via N26 interface (if interworking is supported), allowing coordination between MME and AMF.

results.question: What triggers the mandatory inclusion of the NID IE based on the 5GS mobile identity?
results.reference: The trigger is a mismatch between the SNPN that allocated the 5G-GUTI contained within the 5GS mobile identity IE and the SNPN to which the registration procedure is being performed.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.36, NID
results.model_answer: The mandatory inclusion of the Network Identity (NID) IE is triggered when the 5GS mobile identity type is 'Home Network Identifier (HNI)' or 'Non-3GPP Home Node Identifier (non-3GPP HNI)', as these identities require network identification to uniquely identify the home network.

results.question: What actions should the AMF take upon the fifth expiry of timer T3560 during an EAP-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure?
results.reference: The AMF shall abort the EAP-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure and any ongoing 5GMM specific procedure, and release the N1 NAS signalling connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The AMF shall abort the EAP-based authentication and key agreement procedure upon the fifth expiry of timer T3560.

results.question: How does the AMF handle the scenario where the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message cannot be delivered due to an intra AMF handover, and the target TA is included in the TAI list?
results.reference: Upon successful completion of the intra AMF handover, the AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: If the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message cannot be delivered due to an intra-AMF handover and the target TA is included in the TAI list, the AMF cancels the ongoing authentication procedure and does not re-initiate authentication. The assumption is that the UE remains authenticated after successful handover, and security context may be retrieved or re-established via NAS security mode control upon connection re-establishment.

results.question: What is the procedure for the AMF when a failure of the handover procedure is reported by the lower layer and the N1 NAS signalling connection still exists?
results.reference: The AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: When a failure of the handover procedure is reported by the lower layer and the N1 NAS signalling connection still exists, the AMF shall maintain the N1 NAS signalling connection and may initiate UE context release or other appropriate procedures based on local policy or network conditions.

results.question: Upon the first expiry of timer T3560, what actions must the AMF perform regarding the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and timer T3560?
results.reference: The AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and shall reset and start timer T3560.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: Upon the first expiry of timer T3560, the AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and restart timer T3560.

results.question: What is the required action for both the UE and the network when encountering an unknown IE that is not marked for comprehension?
results.reference: Both shall ignore the unknown Information Element.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.6.1, IEIs unknown in the message
results.model_answer: Both the UE and the network shall ignore an Information Element (IE) that is not marked for comprehension when it is unknown.

results.question: What is the functional relationship between the two 5GMM modes and the N1 NAS signalling connection?
results.reference: The two 5GMM modes, IDLE and CONNECTED, are functionally defined by the absence or presence, respectively, of the N1 NAS signalling connection. The connection's establishment moves the UE to CONNECTED mode, while its release returns the UE to IDLE mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.1, 5GMM modes and N1 NAS signalling connection
results.model_answer: The two 5GMM (5G Mobility Management) modes, 5GMM-IDLE and 5GMM-CONNECTED, define the UE's registration and reachability state with the network and determine whether an N1 NAS signalling connection is established. In 5GMM-IDLE mode, there is no N1 NAS signalling connection; the UE is registered but not reachable at the NAS level without paging. In 5GMM-CONNECTED mode, an N1 NAS signalling connection is established between the UE and the AMF, enabling direct NAS message exchange.

results.question: What is the purpose of the network-requested PDU session modification procedure regarding header compression?
results.reference: The procedure enables the network to re-negotiate the header compression configuration associated with a PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The purpose of the network-requested PDU session modification procedure regarding header compression is to enable the network to modify the QoS flow parameters, including the packet filter and reflective QoS attribute, which may impact header compression behavior at the UE, particularly when ROHC (Robust Header Compression) is applied based on updated QoS rules or PDRs.

results.question: What condition must be met for an SMF supporting NB-N1 mode to apply the specific timer calculation rule?
results.reference: The SMF must be performing NAS signalling with a UE that is using NB-N1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.18, 5GS session management in NB-N1 mode
results.model_answer: The condition that must be met for an SMF supporting NB-N1 mode to apply the specific timer calculation rule is that the PDU session type is Non-IP and the SSC mode is SSC mode 3.

results.question: How does the AMF indicate that general NAS level mobility management congestion control is currently active?
results.reference: The AMF indicates this by including the T3346 value information element in a NAS message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.18.3, T3346 value
results.model_answer: The AMF indicates that general NAS level mobility management congestion control is currently active by setting the 'MICO' (Mobile Initiated Connection Only) mode in the Registration Accept message, and optionally including the 'Service Area List' to restrict the UE's mobility. Additionally, during congestion, the AMF may refrain from sending reachability or paging responses, and implicitly enforce control by rejecting mobility-related procedures with appropriate cause values such as 'congestion'.

results.question: What are the two primary purposes of the service-level authentication and authorization procedure when establishing a PDU session?
results.reference: The procedure is used to authenticate the upper layers of the UE and to authorize the upper layers of the UE when establishing the PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.model_answer: The two primary purposes of the service-level authentication and authorization procedure when establishing a PDU session are: 1) to authenticate the UE at the application or service layer, beyond initial NAS authentication, and 2) to authorize the specific service request (e.g., PDU session type, requested S-NSSAI, or DNN) based on subscription data and network policies.

results.question: Under what condition is the service-level authentication and authorization procedure explicitly prohibited?
results.reference: The procedure shall not be performed during or after the UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure establishing an emergency PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.model_answer: The service-level authentication and authorization procedure is explicitly prohibited if the UE is in a state where it does not have valid registration or has only emergency registration.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 4.10.2: 'Service request procedure shall not be used for emergency services or for establishing connectivity for mobile terminated services when the UE has only emergency registration.'

results.question: How is a successful service-level-AA response delivered to the UE when the procedure is performed for re-authentication on an established PDU session?
results.reference: The successful service-level-AA response is transported from the network to the UE as part of the network-requested PDU session modification procedure in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.model_answer: A successful service-level authorization assurance (AA) response during re-authentication on an established PDU session is delivered via the PDU Session Modification Command message sent by the 5GC to the UE, which includes the 'Authorized QoS flow parameters' and confirms successful re-authentication at the service level.

results.question: What does the UE do with a service-level-AA response received in a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message?
results.reference: The UE passes the service-level-AA response to the upper layer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a service-level-AA (Authentication and Authorization) response in a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message, the UE shall treat it as an indication that network slice-specific authentication/authorization is required. The UE shall initiate an AAuth procedure via the Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate Request service operation for the corresponding Network Slice Instance (NSI), as specified in TS 24.501.

results.question: What two successful actions by the external DN trigger the inclusion of the EAP message information element?
results.reference: The successful authentication and successful authorization of the UE performed by the external DN using EAP trigger the inclusion of this IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.8, EAP message
results.model_answer: The two successful actions by the external DN that trigger the inclusion of the EAP message information element are successful EAP authentication and successful key agreement.

results.question: How does the external DN's use of EAP relate to the presence of the EAP message information element?
results.reference: The EAP message IE is present specifically as a result of the external DN utilizing the EAP protocol to successfully authenticate and authorize the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.8, EAP message
results.model_answer: The presence of the EAP message information element in a 5G NAS message is conditional upon the use of EAP for authentication, including when an external DN-AAA server is involved. If EAP is used, the EAP message IE carries the EAP packet between the UE and the AUSF/AAA server via NAS transport; its presence is required in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST and AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE messages when EAP authentication is performed.

results.question: What role does the external DN play in the scenario that leads to the EAP message IE being included?
results.reference: The external DN plays the active role of performing and successfully completing UE authentication and authorization using EAP, which is the prerequisite for including the IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.8, EAP message
results.model_answer: The external DN (Distinguished Name) is used during EAP-based authentication and key agreement procedures, particularly when the UE or network requests certificate-based authentication. The EAP Message IE is included in NAS messages to transport EAP packets between the UE and the Unified Data Management (UDM) via the Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF). The presence of an external DN typically indicates that the UDM/AUSF expects a client certificate containing that DN during EAP-TLS or similar EAP methods. Thus, the need to exchange EAP messages arises when the authentication framework requires verification of a certificate associated with the external DN, prompting inclusion of the EAP Message IE in Registration Request or Authentication Response messages.

results.question: How does the NAS protocol handle uplink user data packets in a PDU session with IPv4v6 PDU session type?
results.reference: The NAS protocol enables different forwarding treatments of UL user data packets in one or more QoS flows based on signalled QoS rules, derived QoS rules, or any combination of them.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.model_answer: The NAS protocol does not handle uplink user data packets directly in an IPv4v6 PDU session. Instead, NAS is responsible for signaling related to PDU session establishment, modification, and release. Once the PDU session is established, user data (including IPv4 and IPv6 packets) is transported via the user plane over AS layer protocols (e.g., IP over NG-U), not via NAS messages. NAS may trigger procedures (e.g., Service Request) to re-establish user plane connectivity if needed.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 4.5.2: 'The NAS protocol is a non-access stratum protocol and is used between the UE and the AMF for mobility management and session management purposes. It does not carry user data.'

results.question: Why are all uplink user data packets associated with the same QoS flow in an Unstructured PDU session type?
results.reference: In a PDU session of Unstructured PDU session type, all UL user data packets are associated with the same QoS flow as specified by the protocol.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.model_answer: In an Unstructured PDU session type, there is no inherent data unit addressing or ordering, and the network does not apply any user plane protocol. Therefore, all uplink user data packets are inherently treated as belonging to the same QoS flow because the Unstructured PDU session supports only a single QoS flow without discrimination based on packet filters.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 8.3.1: 'For an Unstructured PDU Session, there is no support of multiple QoS flows in the user plane, and traffic mapping to a QoS flow cannot be performed based on packet filters.'

results.question: What mechanism allows for differentiated forwarding of uplink packets in an Ethernet PDU session?
results.reference: The NAS protocol enables different forwarding treatments based on signalled QoS rules, derived QoS rules, or any combination of them for UL user data packets in one or more QoS flows.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.model_answer: The mechanism that allows for differentiated forwarding of uplink packets in an Ethernet PDU session is the Ethernet Header Compression (EHC) with Packet Filter Set (PFS) based on Ethernet parameters such as destination MAC address, source MAC address, and EtherType.

results.question: How does the treatment of uplink user data packets differ between an IPv6 PDU session and an Unstructured PDU session?
results.reference: In an IPv6 PDU session, the NAS protocol enables different forwarding treatments across multiple QoS flows using QoS rules, whereas in an Unstructured PDU session, all UL packets are associated with the same QoS flow.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.5.1.1.1, General
results.model_answer: In an IPv6 PDU session, uplink user data packets are routed based on IPv6 addressing and require IP-based forwarding by the network. In contrast, an Unstructured PDU session does not interpret packet contents; it treats user data as opaque byte streams without any IP header processing, enabling transport of non-IP data with no routing semantics.

results.question: How does a voice-centric UE in 5GMM-REGISTERED state determine when to initiate the establishment of a PDU session for IMS signalling?
results.reference: The UE receives a request from upper layers to establish the PDU session for IMS signalling when IMS voice is available over either 3GPP or non-3GPP access and the conditions for performing an initial registration with IMS specified in 3GPP TS 24.229 subclause U.3.1.2 are satisfied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.model_answer: A voice-centric UE in 5GMM-REGISTERED state determines to initiate the establishment of a PDU session for IMS signalling based on local configuration or operator policies, typically upon power-on or when no active IMS PDU session exists, to ensure VoNR or VoLTE service availability. The UE may use stored provisioning parameters (e.g., from UICC or device settings) indicating the need for an IMS PDU session. This is often triggered during initial registration or mobility registration update if IMS voice over PS session support is required and no suitable PDU session is active.

results.question: What specific rule must a TWIF acting on behalf of an N5CW device follow when allocating a PDU session ID for a new PDU session establishment request?
results.reference: The TWIF acting on behalf of the N5CW device must allocate the 'PDU session identity value 15' for the new PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.model_answer: When a Trusted Wireless IP Access (TWIF) acts on behalf of an N5CW device, it must allocate a PDU session ID that is unique within the context of the UE's PDU sessions for the current registration. The TWIF shall assign a PDU session ID value from the range 1 to 254 and ensure it does not reuse an ID already in use by any existing PDU session for that UE.

results.question: Under what three conditions must the SMF initiate the UUAA-SM procedure instead of immediately accepting or rejecting a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message containing a Service-level-AA container?
results.reference: The SMF must initiate the UUAA-SM procedure when: a) service-level authentication and authorization by the external DN is required due to local policy, b) there is valid user subscription information for the requested DNN (or DNN and S-NSSAI), and c) the Service-level-AA container includes CAA-level UAV ID.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF must initiate the UUAA-SM (User-Plane or Control-Plane Assistance Information for Service-level Authorization and Authentication) procedure instead of immediately accepting or rejecting a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST with a Service-level-AA container when: (1) the SMF receives a Service-level-AA container in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST, (2) the SMF is configured to perform service-level authorization, and (3) the SMF does not have sufficient information to authorize the requested service without additional assistance from the AMF or other NFs.

results.question: How does the UE's NAS perspective generally treat procedures and messages for 5GMM and 5GSM when comparing non-3GPP access to 3GPP access?
results.reference: From the UE's NAS perspective, the procedures and messages defined for 5GMM and 5GSM are generally used in the same way over non-3GPP access as they are over 3GPP access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.1, General
results.model_answer: From the UE's NAS perspective, the procedures and messages for 5GMM and 5GSM are generally treated identically regardless of whether the access is via 3GPP or non-3GPP. The NAS layer is designed to be access-agnostic, ensuring consistent signaling behavior across access types.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 4.2.2: 'The NAS protocols are independent of the access technology used. The same NAS messages and procedures apply for both 3GPP access and non-3GPP access.'

results.question: Why might a UE's NAS experience differences when operating over non-3GPP access despite the general rule for 5GMM and 5GSM procedures?
results.reference: Although the general rule is that procedures and messages are used the same way, a number of specific aspects are different for non-3GPP access, as detailed in subsequent subclauses.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.1, General
results.model_answer: A UE may experience NAS differences over non-3GPP access due to variations in authentication, security establishment, and mobility procedures that are specific to the access type, even though 5GMM and 5GSM procedures are generally consistent across access types. Non-3GPP access uses EAP-based authentication and different key derivation, leading to potential procedural divergences.

results.question: How does the clause qualify its general statement about NAS procedures over non-3GPP access?
results.reference: It qualifies the general statement by noting that there are a number of aspects which are different, and these differences are described in the following subclauses.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.7.1, General
results.model_answer: The clause qualifies its general statement about NAS procedures over non-3GPP access by specifying that, unless otherwise stated, the same NAS procedures apply to both 3GPP and non-3GPP accesses when the UE is registered for 5G services via non-3GPP access, ensuring consistency in NAS operation across access types.

results.question: How does the 5GMM sublayer interact with upper layers when receiving a request to establish a NAS signalling connection?
results.reference: The 5GMM sublayer forwards the request to the lower layers to establish the RRC connection, as it acts as an intermediary between upper layers and lower layers for NAS signalling connection establishment.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.2.9, Interaction with upper layers
results.model_answer: The 5GMM sublayer interacts with upper layers by receiving a request to establish a NAS signalling connection via the N1 interface from the AS layer (e.g., RRC), then initiates NAS signalling procedures such as the Registration Procedure or Service Request Procedure. It provides connection management services to the upper NAS layers (e.g., 5GSM) by establishing, maintaining, and releasing the NAS signalling connection as needed.

results.question: Under what specific condition is the Allowed SSC mode IE included in a network response?
results.reference: The IE is included when the network rejects a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST with the specific cause '#68 "not supported SSC mode"'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.3.3, Allowed SSC mode
results.model_answer: The Allowed SSC mode IE is included in a network response when the network accepts the SSC mode requested by the UE and decides to indicate the allowed SSC modes for future PDU session establishment or modification.

results.question: How does the network use the Allowed SSC mode IE when rejecting a session establishment?
results.reference: The network includes the IE to convey information about allowed SSC modes when rejecting the request due to an unsupported SSC mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.3.3, Allowed SSC mode
results.model_answer: When the network rejects a session establishment, it may include the Allowed SSC mode IE in the PDU Session Establishment Reject message to indicate which SSC modes are permitted for retry by the UE. This allows the UE to reattempt session establishment using an allowed SSC mode, improving the chance of success without requiring explicit signaling beyond the rejection.

results.question: What triggers the inclusion of the Allowed SSC mode IE according to the clause?
results.reference: The trigger is the network's decision to reject a PDU session establishment request with cause value #68, indicating the requested SSC mode is not supported.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.3.3, Allowed SSC mode
results.model_answer: The inclusion of the Allowed SSC mode IE is triggered by the network to indicate which SSC modes are permitted for use by the UE in the registered PLMN. It is included in the Registration Accept message when the network wishes to restrict or allow specific SSC modes for the UE.

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to clause 8.3.2.10?
results.reference: It is included when the network needs to transmit protocol data to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.10, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended protocol configuration options IE is included in a message when the network or the UE needs to transfer additional configuration parameters not supported by the standard protocol configuration options, and it is used only if explicitly allowed by the message definition in clause 8.3.2.10 of TS 24.501.

results.question: What is the purpose of the Extended protocol configuration options IE as defined in clause 8.3.2.10?
results.reference: Its purpose is to allow the network to send protocol data, such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events, to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.2.10, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The purpose of the Extended Protocol Configuration Options (EPCO) IE is to allow the transfer of operator-specific or extended configuration parameters between the UE and the network during mobility management and session management procedures, supporting protocols not covered by the standard Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) and enabling enhanced flexibility in parameter negotiation.

results.question: In what specific case is the network prohibited from using the NOTIFICATION message to re-establish user-plane resources for PDU sessions associated with non-3GPP access over 3GPP access?
results.reference: The network is prohibited if all the PDU sessions of the UE that are established over the 3GPP access are associated with control plane only indication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The network is prohibited from using the NOTIFICATION message to re-establish user-plane resources for PDU sessions associated with non-3GPP access over 3GPP access when the PDU session was established over non-3GPP access and the UE has moved to 3GPP access, but the network has not yet performed an inter-system change of user-plane path via the N2 interface (i.e., no N2-based handover or user-plane relocation has been completed).
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 8.2.27: 'The NOTIFICATION message shall not be used to trigger the re-establishment of the user plane for a PDU session that was established over non-3GPP access if the UE has moved to 3GPP access and the user plane has not been relocated via N2 procedures.'

results.question: What three conditions must all be true for the network to be prohibited from using the NOTIFICATION message over non-3GPP access?
results.reference: The three conditions are: a) the MUSIM UE supports the paging indication for voice services, b) the network has indicated 'paging indication for voice services supported' to the UE, and c) the AMF detects that the downlink data is related to voice service.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.6.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The network is prohibited from using the NOTIFICATION message over non-3GPP access if all of the following conditions are true: (1) the registration was initiated over non-3GPP access, (2) the registration type is mobility registration update, and (3) the UE did not include the 'additional information requested' IE in the Registration Request message.

results.question: Under what conditions must the SMF set the Authorized QoS rules IE in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message when initiating a network-requested PDU session modification?
results.reference: The SMF must set the Authorized QoS rules IE when the authorized QoS rules of the PDU session are modified or are marked as to be synchronized with the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF must set the Authorized QoS rules IE in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message when there are authorized QoS rules to be provided to the UE, particularly when the network has established or modified QoS flows that require conveying the authorized QoS rules for reflective QoS or policy enforcement at the UE side.

results.question: How must the SMF handle service data flows for which the UE has requested traffic segregation if they have different QoS handling?
results.reference: The SMF must bind all these service data flows to a single QoS flow.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF must ensure that service data flows with different QoS handling and for which traffic segregation has been requested by the UE are mapped to separate PDU sessions to maintain isolation and meet distinct QoS requirements.

results.question: What must the SMF ensure regarding packet filters when setting the Authorized QoS rules IE for a PDU session?
results.reference: The SMF must ensure that the number of packet filters used in the authorized QoS rules does not exceed the maximum number of packet filters supported by the UE for that PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF must ensure that packet filters within the Authorized QoS rules are non-ambiguous and non-overlapping, such that each UL or DL packet matches at most one packet filter from the set of authorized QoS rules for the PDU session.

results.question: When the network-requested PDU session modification is triggered for P-CSCF restoration, and the UE had previously requested P-CSCF addresses which were provided, what must the SMF include in the Extended protocol configuration options IE?
results.reference: The SMF must include the P-CSCF IP address(es) in the Extended protocol configuration options IE of the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.2, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The SMF must include the P-CSCF server IPv4 and/or IPv6 address(es) in the Extended protocol configuration options IE to restore the IP-CAN session continuity for IMS signaling.

results.question: What are the two distinct scenarios in which the AMF sets the PRTI IE in a RELAY KEY REJECT message, and what determines which value is used?
results.reference: The AMF sets the PRTI IE to either the PRTI value from the received RELAY KEY REQUEST message if the network decides to reject that request, or to the PRTI value from the received RELAY AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message if the AMF receives an EAP-failure message from the AUSF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The AMF sets the PRTI IE in a RELAY KEY REJECT message in two distinct scenarios: (1) when the relayed registration request from the UE could not be authenticated or authorized via the relay, and (2) when the target NG-RAN node cannot support relayed services. The value of the PRTI IE is determined by the type of relay identity used—either a 5G-GUTI-based or a SUPI-based pseudonym—as specified in clause 8.3.4 of TS 24.501.

results.question: How does the content of the RELAY KEY REJECT message differ when the AMF receives an EAP-failure message from the AUSF compared to when the network decides to reject the RELAY KEY REQUEST?
results.reference: When the AMF receives an EAP-failure message from the AUSF, it includes the EAP message IE set with an EAP-failure message in the RELAY KEY REJECT message. When the network decides to reject the RELAY KEY REQUEST, there is no mention of including an EAP message IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The RELAY KEY REJECT message contains the same mandatory IE, cause, regardless of whether the rejection is due to receiving an EAP-failure from the AUSF or a network-initiated decision. The cause value may differ based on context: 'EAP failure' (cause #41) when linked to EAP-failure, or other appropriate causes (e.g., #40 'Invalid UE parameters') for network-based rejections. No additional IEs are defined in RELAY KEY REJECT to distinguish the source of rejection.

results.question: What are the sequential actions the AMF must take when the UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure is not accepted?
results.reference: The AMF must 1) create a RELAY KEY REJECT message, 2) set its PRTI IE based on the specific rejection scenario, and 3) send the RELAY KEY REJECT message to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: When the UE-initiated authentication and key agreement (AKA) procedure is not accepted, the AMF must send an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to the UE, optionally followed by an OPTIONAL IDENTITY REQUEST if additional identification is needed. The AMF shall then terminate the NAS signaling connection and may initiate implicit de-registration of the UE.

results.question: What is the consequence for the UE upon receiving a RELAY KEY REJECT message, and what subsequent action must it take?
results.reference: The UE must consider the authentication has failed and must perform the PC5 signalling protocol procedure as specified in 3GPP 24.554 subclause 7.2.2.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.5, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a RELAY KEY REJECT message, the UE shall abort the relay key establishment procedure and may proceed with normal NAS signaling for registration or service request if needed. The UE shall not attempt to establish a relay key again unless triggered by a new condition or explicit network indication.

results.question: How does the AMF determine the value of the non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer when T3346 is greater than the non-3GPP de-registration timer in specific NAS messages?
results.reference: The AMF sets the non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer value to be 8 minutes greater than the value of timer T3346 when T3346 is greater than the non-3GPP de-registration timer and the T3346 value IE is provided in DEREGISTRATION REQUEST (with 3GPP access type), REGISTRATION REJECT during mobility/periodic registration update, or SERVICE REJECT messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.7, Handling of the periodic registration update timer and mobile reachable timer
results.model_answer: The AMF does not use a non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer value that exceeds the value of T3346. When T3346 is greater than the configured non-3GPP de-registration timer, the AMF effectively applies the larger value (T3346) as it controls the waiting period before allowing re-registration; thus, the effective implicit de-registration behavior is bound by T3346.

results.question: Under what condition does the UE reset and start the non-3GPP de-registration timer, and when is this timer stopped?
results.reference: The UE registered over non-3GPP access resets and starts the non-3GPP de-registration timer when the N1 NAS signalling connection over non-3GPP access is released. The timer is stopped when certain NAS messages are received or when specific conditions are met, as indicated by the ellipsis in the clause.

results.question: What triggers the AMF to start a non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer for a UE registered over non-3GPP access?
results.reference: The AMF starts a non-3GPP implicit de-registration timer for the UE registered over non-3GPP access when the N1 NAS signalling connection over non-3GPP access is released.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.3.7, Handling of the periodic registration update timer and mobile reachable timer
